analysis.subject: biology
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers heterozygosity and allele frequency definitions, genotype counting with k(k+1)/2 and homozygous versus heterozygous expectations, Punnett squares, gene pool and fitness, and distribution of human genetic diversity within and between populations.

overview.headline: Heterozygosity and allele frequency shape genetic diversity in populations

keyPoints.point: Allele frequency is used to estimate the frequency of a given genetic profile at a locus
keyPoints.quote: Allele frequency, or the frequency at which alleles are found at any locus of interest, is used to estimate the frequency of a given genetic profile.

keyPoints.point: Heterozygosity across loci serves as a general indicator of genetic variability
keyPoints.quote: The measure of the amount of heterozygosity across loci can be used as a general indicator of the amount of genetic variability.

keyPoints.point: Parameter k represents the expected number of homozygous genotypes at a locus
keyPoints.quote: The parameter k also represents the expected number of homozygous genotypes

keyPoints.point: Human genetic diversity comes from individuals of same population accounting for most variation
keyPoints.quote: The study of genetics has revealed that approximately 85% of human genetic diversity comes from individuals of the same population.

keyTerms.gloss: having two different alleles at a specific locus
keyTerms.quote: If an individual has two different alleles at a specific locus, the individual is heterozygous at that locus

keyTerms.gloss: having two identical alleles that are the same at a locus
keyTerms.quote: if the two alleles are the same, the individual is homozygous.

keyTerms.gloss: unique set of alleles found across members of a species or population
keyTerms.quote: A gene pool is the unique set of alleles that could be found by analyzing the DNA from every member of a species or population.

keyTerms.gloss: probability of transmitting genes to next generation relative to average for population
keyTerms.quote: Fitness is the probability of transmitting one's genes to the next generation in relation to the average probability for that population.

keyTerms.gloss: measure of genetic variability indicated by heterozygosity across loci
keyTerms.quote: The measure of the amount of heterozygosity across loci can be used as a general indicator of the amount of genetic variability.

keyTerms.gloss: frequency at which alleles are found at a locus used to estimate genetic profile frequency
keyTerms.quote: Allele frequency, or the frequency at which alleles are found at any locus of interest, is used to estimate the frequency of a given genetic profile.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Builds checkable recall of core definitions like diploid inheritance and heterozygosity before applying counts
componentPlan.focusQuote: Every diploid cell has two alleles, one inherited from each parent.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Groups genotype categories by expected counts to distinguish homozygous and heterozygous types using the k formula
componentPlan.focusQuote: parameter k also represents the expected number of homozygous genotypes, and k[(k-1)/2] represents the expected number of heterozygous genotypes.
